chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ghalib al-Shafi`i narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad Mujahid ibn A`yun ibn Dawud informed us, saying: `Isa ibn Ahmad al-`Asqalani informed us, saying: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayyil informed us, saying: Israfil informed us, saying: Thuwayr narrated from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
There is not a verse in the Qur'an more beloved to me than the Word of the Mighty and High:
Surely Allah does not forgive that anything should be associated with Him, and forgives what is beside that to whomsoever He pleases.

key_terms.أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ: That He be associated with partners
key_terms.وَيَغْفُرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ: And forgives what is besides that

ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved verse in the Quran according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam Ali (AS) highlights the supremacy of Tawhid by identifying the verse on Shirk as the most beloved, emphasizing that while Allah may forgive all other sins, He does not forgive Shirk if one dies upon it. This selection underscores the foundational Shia theological principle that the preservation of divine unity is the primary criterion for spiritual success and divine mercy. The emphasis on 'what He wills' for other sins reflects the balance between divine justice and grace, central to Shia exegesis.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ghalib al-Shafi``I said: Abu Muhammad ibn Mujahid ibn A`yun ibn Dawwud reported to us that `Isa ibn Ahmad al-`Asqalani reported to us that al-Nadr ibn Shumayyil reported to us that Israfil reported to us that Thuwayr reported, on the authority of his father that `Ali (AS) said:
There is not a verse in the Qur`an more beloved to me that the Word of the Mighty and High:
Surely Allah does not forgive that anything should be associated with Him, and forgives what is beside that to whomsoever He pleases.
